Name: Adobe Workfront
Vendor: Adobe Inc. Public company (NASDAQ: ADBE), headquartered in San Jose, California, US; Adobe bought Workfront of Lehi, Utah for $1.5 billion in December 2020.
Market_Evidence: More than 3,000 customers and one million users when Adobe agreed to buy it in November 2020 (KMWorld, 12 November 2020); now a product line of Adobe, a large public company.
Price_Note: Adobe publishes no prices: Workflow Select, Prime and Ultimate packages are sold by quote, with Standard, Light and Contributor licences priced separately.
Free_Plan_Note: No free plan; Adobe offers demos, and a free 60-day Workfront Planning trial ran from 2 March to 1 May 2026 for existing Workflow customers.
Plans: Workflow Select, Workflow Prime and Workflow Ultimate, plus Planning Select, Prime and Ultimate and Workfront Fusion automation, all quote-only; older customers may still hold the legacy Select, Prime and Ultimate packages.
Integrations_Note: Workfront Fusion, Adobe’s own integration platform, lists over 70 connectors (Adobe Experience Manager, Creative Cloud, Salesforce, Jira, Slack, Microsoft Teams among them) and is metered by operations; a full REST API and event subscriptions sit beside it, and an MCP server was added in 2026.
Hosting: Adobe-run multi-tenant clusters in cloud providers’ data centres. Adobe’s Experience Cloud hosting-locations page (updated 5 November 2026) shows Workfront core processing and storage sites in Oregon, California, Iowa and Virginia in the US and in Ireland, the Netherlands and Germany in the EU, with the location provisioned at contract signing. No Asia-Pacific site, and no self-managed or on-premise edition.
Security: Covered by Adobe Experience Cloud’s SOC 2 Type II, SOC 3, ISO 27001:2022, ISO 27017 and ISO 27018 certifications and HIPAA-ready status; not FedRAMP. SSO and user provisioning through the Adobe Admin Console on every package; environment promotion needs Prime or Ultimate, and business rules and Data Connect need Workflow Ultimate. Customer-managed encryption keys are not documented.
Calendar_Sync: None current. The Outlook two-way sync on the legacy Home calendar went with Legacy Home in October 2024, and Workfront for Outlook stopped working when Microsoft disabled legacy Exchange tokens on 1 October 2025. No Google Calendar integration or iCal feed is documented.
Data_Out: Reports and lists export to PDF, Excel (.xls up to 65,000 rows, .xlsx up to 100,000), CSV and tab-delimited (50,000 rows); dashboards only to PDF. Full REST API; Data Connect warehouse access on Ultimate. Kick-Starts import and export via Excel.
Platforms: Web; Adobe Workfront apps for iOS and Android; Workfront View for iPad.
AI: AI Assistant on Select or higher with a Standard licence and a signed Adobe Gen AI agreement; it summarises work and writes formulas, and is being replaced by CX Enterprise Coworker from September 2026. AI Collaborators (agents assignable to tasks) became generally available in August 2026. Adobe says customer data is not used to train the Azure OpenAI models behind AI Assistant.
Value_for_money_Review: Every package and licence type is quote-only, with no free plan and automation through Fusion metered separately.
Ease_of_use_Review: Access levels, licence types, custom forms and templates need a trained administrator before a team is productive.
Enterprise_features_Review: Adobe Admin Console identity, granular access levels, portfolios, programs, resource planning and Experience Cloud certifications.
Interface_flexibility_Review: Gantt with critical path, boards, calendar reports, dashboards, custom forms, Fusion automation and a separate Planning product.
Data_control_Review: SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 under Experience Cloud, US or EU hosting set at contract, but no self-managed edition.
Portability_Review: Report exports to Excel, CSV and TSV stop at 50,000 to 100,000 rows; the REST API is the realistic route out.
Summary: Adobe Workfront runs projects, incoming requests, proofing and approvals, timesheets and portfolio planning in one tenant. It is bought by large marketing, creative and operations departments, often alongside Adobe’s Creative Cloud and Experience Cloud. Work is organised as portfolios, programs, projects, tasks and issues, with Gantt charts that show predecessors and the critical path, Kanban and Scrum boards, calendar reports and a resource planner. Workfront Planning adds a separate record-based layer for campaign and strategy planning. Calendar sync is now missing: the legacy Home calendar’s Outlook link was removed in October 2024 and the Outlook add-in stopped working in October 2025. There is no published price and no free plan. Adobe sells Workflow Select, Prime and Ultimate packages by quote, with Standard, Light and Contributor licences; strategic portfolio planning and environment promotion start at Prime, Data Connect and business rules at Ultimate, and Planning and Fusion are separate purchases. Workfront falls under Adobe Experience Cloud’s SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 scope, with data held in the US or in the EU (Ireland, the Netherlands, Germany) as set in the contract. AI Assistant requires a signed Adobe Gen AI agreement and is turning into CX Enterprise Coworker from September 2026. Leaving means row-capped report exports or the REST API.
Caveat: Prices are never published, and Adobe reorganised packaging into separate Workflow, Planning and Automation purchases, so quotes from older comparisons may not match what is sold in 2026.

Name: Asana
Vendor: Asana, Inc. Publicly listed on the NYSE (ASAN); headquartered in San Francisco, United States.
Market_Evidence: Asana reported revenue of $790.8 million for fiscal 2026 (year to 31 January 2026), with 25,928 customers spending $5,000 or more a year, per its results release of 2 March 2026.
Price_Note: Starter, per user per month billed annually; $13.49 billed monthly. Paid plans start at 2 seats, added one at a time up to 5 users, then in steps of 5 up to 30, 10 up to 100, 25 up to 500 and 50 beyond.
Free_Plan_Note: Personal is free for 1 or 2 people with unlimited tasks and projects in list, board and calendar views; no timeline, automations, custom fields or dashboards.
Plans: Personal free (up to 2 users); Starter $10.99 annual or $13.49 monthly; Advanced $24.99 annual or $30.49 monthly; Enterprise and Enterprise+ by quote.
Integrations_Note: The app directory lists several hundred apps, including Slack, Microsoft Teams, Google Drive, Salesforce, Jira Cloud, GitHub, Zoom, Power BI, Zapier and Claude; a public REST API with webhooks is documented at developers.asana.com.
Hosting: Asana-operated cloud, US by default; data residency in Europe, Australia or Japan on Enterprise+. No self-managed or on-premise edition.
Security: SOC 2 Type II, SOC 3, ISO/IEC 27001, 27017, 27018 and 27701, CSA STAR Level 1, HIPAA support. SAML SSO and SCIM on Enterprise; audit logs, SIEM integration and EKM on Enterprise+.
Calendar_Sync: One-way: iCal subscription links for a project or My Tasks (tasks need a due date), and an Outlook Calendar integration that sends Asana changes to Outlook but not back. Available on all plans.
Data_Out: Per-project CSV (no comments or attachments) and JSON export; a full organisation export as JSON, with optional attachments, only on Enterprise+ and legacy Enterprise. Public REST API with webhooks; CSV importer.
Platforms: Web, iOS, Android, desktop apps for macOS and Windows.
AI: Asana AI, AI Teammates and AI Studio on all paid plans with 5 requests per user per month (capped per account) and monthly AI Studio credits; extra requests are paid. Asana states it does not use customer data for training and contractually bars its AI partners from doing so.
Value_for_money_Review: Free for only two people since late 2025, then $10.99 a seat with timeline, and $24.99 for time tracking.
Ease_of_use_Review: Tasks, sections and My Tasks are quick to learn; portfolios, goals and rules take deliberate setup.
Enterprise_features_Review: SAML and SCIM on Enterprise, audit logs, SIEM and residency on Enterprise+, admin console and ISO 27001 certification.
Interface_flexibility_Review: List, board, calendar, timeline, Gantt, dashboards, portfolios, forms, rules and custom fields, mostly from Starter up.
Data_control_Review: Data residency in Europe, Australia or Japan and customer-held keys through EKM, both on Enterprise+ only.
Portability_Review: Project CSV omits comments; a full organisation JSON export with attachments is reserved for Enterprise+ admins.
Summary: Asana organises work as tasks inside projects, with the same task able to sit in several projects at once. It is sold to whole organisations that want one shared place for team plans, from marketing calendars to cross-functional launches. Every project can be shown as a list, board, calendar, timeline or Gantt chart, and portfolios and goals roll projects up for managers. Rules, forms and custom fields handle routine workflow. Since 2025 Asana has added AI Teammates and AI Studio, which run agents and automations against a monthly allowance of requests and credits. The free Personal plan was cut to two users in November 2025, so a team of three must pay from day one. Starter at $10.99 a seat adds timeline and automations; time tracking, approvals and advanced reporting sit on Advanced at $24.99. Above five users seats are bought in steps of 5, then 10 above 30 users, and AI use beyond the included 5 requests per user per month (up to 50 per account below Enterprise) is charged at $0.50 to $0.60 per request. Asana holds SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001, 27017, 27018 and 27701 certificates. Data residency in Europe, Australia or Japan, customer-managed encryption keys and audit logs come with Enterprise+, and Asana states that neither it nor its AI partners train models on customer data. Projects export to CSV or JSON, but the full organisation export is Enterprise+ only, so leaving a smaller plan means working through the API.
Caveat: Asana cut the free plan to two users in November 2025 and is moving older 10-user free workspaces to the same limit, so free-tier reviews from before then are out of date.

Name: Azure Boards
Vendor: Microsoft. Publicly listed (NASDAQ: MSFT); headquartered in Redmond, Washington, USA. Azure Boards is part of the Azure DevOps Services suite.
Market_Evidence: A service line of Microsoft, a public company; the Visual Studio Marketplace lists 5,436 Azure DevOps extensions, 1,698 of them for Azure Boards (November 2026); Microsoft publishes no separate Azure DevOps user count.
Price_Note: Azure DevOps Basic, per user per month after the first 5 free users, billed monthly through an Azure subscription; no annual rate is published.
Free_Plan_Note: The first 5 Basic users are free with Boards, Repos, one Pipelines job and 2 GiB of Artifacts; unlimited free Stakeholders can view boards and backlogs, add and edit work items and move cards, but cannot reorder backlogs, bulk edit, plan sprints or configure boards.
Plans: Stakeholder free; Basic free for 5 users, then $6 per user per month; Basic + Test Plans $52 per user per month. Visual Studio subscribers and GitHub Enterprise users get Basic at no extra charge.
Integrations_Note: The Visual Studio Marketplace lists 1,698 extensions in the Azure Boards category, plus first-party links to GitHub, Microsoft Teams, Slack, Power BI and Excel; full REST APIs, service hooks and an Azure DevOps MCP Server.
Hosting: Azure datacentres in a geography chosen per organisation: Australia, Brazil, Canada, Asia Pacific, EU, India, UK or US, movable later; profile data follows user location and tokens stay in the US. Azure DevOps Server is the self-managed on-premise edition, patched through October 2026.
Security: ISO 27001:2022, ISO 27018:2019, SOC 1 Type II, SOC 2 Type II, HIPAA with BAA, EU Model Clauses, Germany C5, Australia IRAP and ENS Spain. Sign-in through Microsoft Entra ID with its SSO and conditional access; audit log (in public preview) requires Entra-backed organisations and keeps events 90 days, with streaming to Splunk or Azure.
Calendar_Sync: None. Work items do not publish to Google or Outlook calendars, and there is no iCal feed; Microsoft’s Team Calendar extension tracks sprints and days off rather than work items.
Data_Out: Query results export to CSV and import back for bulk edits; Excel integration publishes flat lists and hierarchies; Analytics views feed Power BI. Full REST APIs and service hooks. The Data Migration Tool moves Server collections into Services; whole-organisation moves elsewhere need Marketplace tools or the API.
Platforms: Web, with Visual Studio and Excel clients; no official mobile app for Boards was found. Azure DevOps Server runs on Windows Server for self-hosting.
AI: GitHub Copilot integration starts Copilot’s coding agent from a work item to create a branch and draft pull request; it requires a GitHub Copilot subscription and GitHub repositories. The Azure DevOps MCP Server, hosted in Europe and the US, passes data through without storing it.
Value_for_money_Review: Five free Basic users, unlimited free Stakeholders and $6 a seat after that, with repos and pipelines in the same licence.
Ease_of_use_Review: Process templates, area and iteration paths and query-driven views need a configured project before a team is comfortable.
Enterprise_features_Review: Entra ID sign-in and conditional access, granular permissions, audit streaming, multi-organisation billing and ISO, SOC, C5 and IRAP coverage.
Interface_flexibility_Review: Backlogs, boards, taskboards, delivery plans, queries, dashboards, Power BI views and custom processes; no calendar or list-style planner.
Data_control_Review: Eight data geographies chosen per organisation, and Azure DevOps Server remains on sale for fully self-managed hosting.
Portability_Review: Query results export to CSV and Excel and the REST API is complete, but no one-click export of a whole organisation exists.
Summary: Azure Boards is the work-tracking part of Microsoft’s Azure DevOps, the successor to Team Foundation Server. It suits software teams already on Azure, GitHub or Visual Studio who want backlogs and sprints beside their code and pipelines. Work items follow Agile, Scrum, CMMI or custom processes and appear in backlogs, Kanban boards, sprint taskboards and saved queries; Delivery Plans show up to 20 team backlogs on a timeline with dependencies, and dashboards and Power BI handle reporting. There is no calendar view, and time is tracked as remaining and completed hours rather than with timesheets. Basic access is free for 5 users and then $6 a seat a month, billed through Azure. Unlimited Stakeholders are free and can edit work items and move cards on a board, but cannot reorder backlogs, plan sprints or configure boards, so whoever plans the work needs a paid seat. Visual Studio and GitHub Enterprise licences include Basic. Organisations choose one of eight geographies, from the EU to India, and Azure DevOps Server still ships for on-premise use, with Patch 9 released in October 2026. Microsoft lists ISO 27001, SOC 2 Type II, HIPAA and C5. AI arrives through GitHub Copilot, which can turn a work item into a draft pull request. Leaving is done by query exports or the API.
Caveat: The audit log is still in public preview and only works for Entra ID-backed organisations, and free Stakeholder seats can edit work items and move cards but cannot reorder backlogs or plan sprints.

Name: Google Tasks
Vendor: Google LLC, a subsidiary of Alphabet Inc. (NASDAQ: GOOGL). Publicly traded, headquartered in Mountain View, California, USA.
Market_Evidence: Google publishes no Tasks user count; the service ships inside Gmail, Google Calendar, Chat, Drive and Docs for every Google account and Workspace customer, a product line of Alphabet (checked November 2026).
Price_Note: No paid tier of its own. Free with any Google account; organisations get admin control, data regions and Gemini features through Google Workspace, from Business Starter at $7 per user per month on an annual plan ($8.40 flexible).
Free_Plan_Note: Every Tasks feature is free with a Google account, up to 100,000 tasks in total and 20,000 open tasks per list; group tasks in Chat spaces and assigning from Docs need an eligible Workspace account.
Plans: Free with a personal Google account; included in every Google Workspace edition (Business Starter $7, Standard $14, Plus $22 per user per month on annual plans), where the administrator controls access.
Integrations_Note: Gmail (email to task), Google Calendar, Chat spaces, Docs, Drive, Keep reminders and Gemini; third parties connect through the public Google Tasks REST API, which has no webhooks.
Hosting: Google’s own data centres. Workspace Business Standard and Plus, Enterprise, Frontline and Education Standard/Plus editions can apply a data region policy to Tasks data at rest; personal accounts have no choice. No self-managed edition.
Security: Google lists Workspace services including Tasks in scope for ISO 27001, 27017, 27018 and SOC 1, 2 and 3. SSO, MFA and audit sit at the Google Workspace account level; administrators control access to Tasks, but Tasks has no roles of its own.
Calendar_Sync: Native: tasks with dates appear in Google Calendar on web and mobile, and edits in either place apply to the same task. Repeating tasks show a limited number of upcoming instances. No Outlook sync and no iCal feed.
Data_Out: Google Takeout exports the whole account’s Tasks as JSON (third-party guides disagree on whether it is one file or one per list), with titles, notes, due dates, completion, order and subtask links; no CSV and no scheduled backups. The Google Tasks REST API reads and writes lists and tasks. No importers.
Platforms: Web (inside Google Calendar and the side panel of Gmail, Chat, Drive, Docs, Sheets and Slides), Android, iOS and ChromeOS. No desktop app for Windows, macOS or Linux.
AI: Gemini in the Workspace side panels can create reminders and to-do lists in Google Tasks since September 2026, on Business and Enterprise Standard and Plus and on Google AI Pro and Ultra. Google states Workspace prompts are customer data and not used for training without permission.
Value_for_money_Review: Free with any Google account and already included in every Workspace plan, with no caps a person is likely to meet.
Ease_of_use_Review: The simplest tool here: a list, a date and a star, reachable from the Gmail and Calendar side panel.
Enterprise_features_Review: Workspace admins can switch Tasks on or off and apply SSO and data regions, but Tasks itself has no roles or reporting.
Interface_flexibility_Review: Lists, subtasks, stars, deadlines and a calendar display; no labels, priorities, board, custom fields or automation.
Data_control_Review: Workspace lists Tasks under ISO 27001 and SOC 2 and data regions from Business Standard; personal accounts get no region choice.
Portability_Review: Google Takeout gives a JSON export of every list and the REST API is free, but there is no CSV or importer.
Summary: Google Tasks is a bare to-do list that lives inside Gmail, Google Calendar and the Workspace side panel, with mobile apps for Android and iOS. It suits people who already plan their day in Google Calendar and want tasks beside their events, not a separate system. A task has a title, details, a start date and time with a duration, a deadline, a repeat rule, a star and subtasks, and sits in a list. Dated tasks show on the Calendar grid, an email can become a task, and Workspace users can assign group tasks in Chat spaces and Docs. There are no labels, priorities, shared lists, board or timeline. There is nothing to buy: a personal Google account gets the whole product. Organisations get it with any Workspace edition, from Business Starter at $7 a user per month on an annual plan, which adds administrator control rather than task features. For Workspace customers Tasks data is covered by Google’s ISO 27001 and SOC 2 scope and by data region policies on Business Standard and above; Gemini can create tasks from any Workspace side panel since September 2026, and Google says prompts are not used for training without permission. Leaving is simple but thin: Takeout gives JSON for the whole account, there is no CSV, and nothing imports in.
Caveat: Google Tasks has had no official feature announcements in 2026 beyond a widget redesign; a search bar and a “Plan your day” view have only appeared in app teardowns.

Name: Jira
Vendor: Atlassian. Publicly listed (NASDAQ: TEAM); founded in Sydney, Australia, in 2002, incorporated in Delaware since 2022, with headquarters in Sydney and San Francisco.
Market_Evidence: Atlassian reported FY2026 revenue of $6,572 million and 350,000+ customers (Q4 FY2026 results, 6 August 2026), with Jira as its flagship product line.
Price_Note: Standard billed annually at $950 a year for the 10-user tier (about $7.92 per user per month; $9,700 for 100 users); monthly billing is $9.70 per user for users 1-100. Prices from 13 October 2026.
Free_Plan_Note: Up to 10 users with 2 GB storage, every core view, 150 automation steps a month and community support; no Rovo AI, permissions or audit log.
Plans: Free for up to 10 users; Standard $9.70 per user a month billed monthly, or $950 a year for 10 users (about $7.92 per user a month); Premium $19.60 per user billed monthly, or $1,950 a year for 10 users; Enterprise annual only, with published list prices from $179,000 a year for 1,000 users. Monthly per-user rates fall in higher user bands.
Integrations_Note: The Atlassian Marketplace lists more than 6,000 Cloud apps (October 2026), including Tempo, GitHub, GitLab, Slack, Microsoft Teams and Figma; public REST APIs, webhooks, the Forge app platform and a Rovo MCP server on paid plans.
Hosting: Atlassian Cloud on AWS. Data residency on Standard, Premium and Enterprise in Australia, Canada, EU, Germany, India, Japan, Singapore, South Korea, Switzerland, UK and USA. Jira Data Center (self-managed) ended sales to new customers on 30 March 2026 and reaches end of life on 28 March 2029; Jira Server lost support on 15 February 2024.
Security: SOC 2 Type II reports, ISO/IEC 27001 and 27018 (scope varies by product), PCI DSS and a GDPR DPA; Atlassian Government Cloud holds FedRAMP Moderate (March 2025). SSO, SCIM and AD sync via Atlassian Guard Standard, included only on Enterprise; site audit logs from Standard, user-activity audit logs on Enterprise. BYOK is closed to new enrolment and replaced by customer-managed keys.
Calendar_Sync: None native. The calendar view shows work items by date inside Jira only; Google, Outlook or iCal sync needs a third-party Marketplace app.
Data_Out: Search results export to CSV or Excel CSV (all or current fields, up to 10,000 items), XML, and Word (descriptions and comments included, about 150 items at a time). Backup Manager produces a full XML site backup including comments, sprints and configuration, with attachments optional (48 hours between such backups); automation rules and app data are excluded. REST APIs and webhooks on all plans; direct importers for Asana and Trello, plus CSV and JSON import.
Platforms: Web, iOS and Android. The official Jira Cloud for Mac app is no longer supported.
AI: Rovo Search, Chat and Agents on Standard, Premium and Enterprise, metered by monthly credits (25, 70 and 150 per user); not on Free. Atlassian says its LLM providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and self-hosted open models) do not store or train on inputs. Separately, from 17 August 2026 Atlassian uses contributed data, de-identified and aggregated, to improve its apps and AI experiences: metadata is always contributed on Free, Standard and Premium and can be turned off only on Enterprise; in-app data is on by default on Free and Standard (admins can turn it off) and off by default on Premium and Enterprise.
Value_for_money_Review: Ten free users and Standard at about $7.92 a user billed annually, but advanced planning needs Premium and SSO needs Atlassian Guard.
Ease_of_use_Review: Schemes, workflows, screens and JQL reward an administrator; newcomers face unfamiliar terms before the first sprint.
Enterprise_features_Review: SAML SSO and SCIM through Guard, audit logs, sandboxes, 150 sites, Atlassian Analytics and FedRAMP Moderate Government Cloud.
Interface_flexibility_Review: Custom workflows and fields on every plan, six views, JQL dashboards, rule automation and 6,000 Marketplace apps.
Data_control_Review: Residency across 11 locations from Standard, but Data Center stopped selling to new customers in March 2026.
Portability_Review: CSV export to 10,000 items, a full XML site backup with attachments and complete REST APIs; the backup only restores into Jira.
Summary: Jira tracks work as issues, now called work items, moving through workflows that an administrator defines, and it remains the default tracker in large software organisations. Atlassian also sells it to marketing, operations and other business teams on the same plans. Every plan has backlog, board, list, timeline, calendar and summary views, custom fields and workflows, and JQL queries that feed dashboards and reports. The timeline shows dependencies within one project; plans across projects, capacity and scenario modelling are Premium. What it lacks out of the box is calendar sync and a timesheet, both of which arrive through the Marketplace. The free plan stops at 10 users and 2 GB. Prices rose by about 7% on 13 October 2026: Standard is $9.70 per user a month billed monthly for the first 100 users, about $7.92 billed annually, and Premium $19.60. Rovo AI is included on paid plans with monthly credit allowances (25, 70 and 150 per user); SSO and SCIM need an Atlassian Guard subscription below Enterprise. Data can be pinned to 11 residency locations from Standard upwards. Since 17 August 2026 Atlassian uses de-identified, aggregated metadata from Free, Standard and Premium sites to improve its apps and AI features, and only Enterprise can switch that off; in-app content is also contributed by default on Free and Standard unless an admin turns it off. Leaving is realistic: CSV, XML and Word exports, a full backup with attachments and complete APIs.
Caveat: Jira Data Center stopped selling to new customers on 30 March 2026 and goes read-only on 28 March 2029, so Cloud is now the only edition a new buyer can choose.

Name: Microsoft Planner
Vendor: Microsoft Corporation. Public company (NASDAQ: MSFT), headquartered in Redmond, Washington, US.
Market_Evidence: Bundled with Microsoft 365 Business Basic, Standard and Premium, Office 365 E1, E3 and E5 and Microsoft 365 A1 (Microsoft Learn, October 2026); Microsoft publishes no Planner-only user count.
Price_Note: Planner Plan 1, per user per month paid annually as listed by Microsoft in October 2026; basic Planner comes with most Microsoft 365 business and enterprise suites at no extra charge.
Free_Plan_Note: No standalone free plan; basic Planner (grid, board, schedule and charts views) is included in Microsoft 365 Business Basic and higher suites, but timeline, goals and sprints need Plan 1.
Plans: Basic Planner inside Microsoft 365 and Office 365 suites; Planner Plan 1 at $10 and Planner and Project Plan 3 at $30 per user per month paid annually. Planner and Project Plan 5 (formerly $55) is still named in Microsoft’s Project for the web service description but no longer on Planner’s subscriptions page, which lists only Plan 1 and Plan 3.
Integrations_Note: Built into Teams, Outlook, To Do, SharePoint and Loop, with Power Automate flows and Power BI reporting on premium plans; the Planner API in Microsoft Graph covers basic plans, premium plans live in Dataverse, and a Planner MCP server is documented.
Hosting: Microsoft Azure. Basic plans are stored by the tenant’s default geography: Europe, Americas or Asia-Pacific macro-regions, with local storage for Australia, Canada, India and Japan (UK tenants map to Europe); Microsoft makes no specific residency commitment for Planner and it does not take part in Advanced Data Residency. Premium plans are stored in Dataverse. No on-premise edition (Project Server is a separate product).
Security: Covered by Microsoft 365’s audit reports on the Service Trust Portal, the Product Terms and the Data Protection Addendum. Sign-in through Microsoft Entra ID with its SSO and provisioning; Purview audit logs on all plans, eDiscovery only for basic group plans, no retention policies, and Purview needs an E5-class licence.
Calendar_Sync: One-way iCalendar publishing of a plan’s schedule to the Outlook calendar (any iCal client can subscribe); assigned tasks also show in Microsoft To Do. No Google Calendar sync and nothing flows back.
Data_Out: Export a plan to Excel from the web app; global admins can export a user’s plans as JSON with the Export-PlannerUserContent PowerShell cmdlet. Planner API in Microsoft Graph for basic plans; premium plan data is reachable through Dataverse. Direct .mpp import was removed when Project for the web retired.
Platforms: Web, Planner in Teams (Windows, macOS, Linux via the Teams client), Outlook integration, iOS and Android apps.
AI: Copilot in Planner and the Planner Agent (Project Manager agent) require a Microsoft 365 Copilot licence, with more capability for Plan 1 or Plan 3 holders. Microsoft states prompts, responses and Microsoft Graph data are not used to train foundation models, and EU traffic stays within the EU Data Boundary.
Value_for_money_Review: Boards come free with most Microsoft 365 suites, but timelines cost $10 a seat and critical path $30.
Ease_of_use_Review: Basic plans are a card board inside Teams and Outlook that most Microsoft 365 users can pick up unaided.
Enterprise_features_Review: Entra ID sign-in, Purview audit logs and eDiscovery, but no Planner admin roles and eDiscovery only for basic group plans.
Interface_flexibility_Review: Grid, board, schedule, charts, timeline, people and goals views, sprints and custom fields, with Power Automate behind premium plans.
Data_control_Review: Data follows the tenant’s geography (Europe, Americas, Asia-Pacific, Australia, Canada, Japan or India), with no residency commitment or customer-managed keys.
Portability_Review: Export to Excel per plan, admin JSON export per user and the Graph API; .mpp import was removed in 2025.
Summary: Microsoft Planner is the task and project tool inside Microsoft 365, reached from the web, Teams and Outlook. Since August 2025 it also carries what used to be Project for the web, so one app now spans a team’s shared board and a scheduled project. Basic plans give tasks with buckets, checklists, labels and attachments in grid, board, schedule and charts views, plus My Day and My Tasks. Premium plans add a timeline (Gantt) view with dependencies, sprints and backlogs, goals, custom fields and a people view; Plan 3 adds critical path, baselines, roadmaps and an assignments view. There is no time tracking, and premium plans top out at 3,000 tasks each. Most organisations already have basic Planner through a Microsoft 365 or Office 365 suite. Planner Plan 1 costs $10 per user per month paid annually and Planner and Project Plan 3 costs $30; Planner’s subscriptions page now lists only those two premium plans, and Project Online retired on 30 September 2026. Copilot and the Planner Agent need a separate Microsoft 365 Copilot licence. Basic plan data sits in Azure in the tenant’s geography and premium plans in Dataverse, under Microsoft’s certifications and data protection addendum; Planner does not take part in Advanced Data Residency or support customer-managed keys. Leaving means Excel exports, an admin PowerShell JSON export or the Graph API.
Caveat: Microsoft’s own price pages blocked automated access for this review; the $10 and $30 figures are Microsoft’s list prices as quoted in October 2026, and no formal end-of-sale notice for Plan 5 was found.

Name: Microsoft To Do
Vendor: Microsoft Corporation. Publicly traded (NASDAQ: MSFT), headquartered in Redmond, Washington, USA; To Do came from the team behind Wunderlist, acquired in 2015.
Market_Evidence: Microsoft publishes no To Do user count; its Graph documentation (updated August 2025) says To Do reaches “millions of users”, and the app ships inside Outlook and Teams for Microsoft 365 work accounts as part of a major public company’s product line.
Price_Note: No paid tier of its own. Free with any personal Microsoft account (Outlook.com, Skype, Xbox); for organisations it comes with Microsoft 365 business, enterprise and education plans that include an Exchange Online mailbox.
Free_Plan_Note: Every feature is free with a personal Microsoft account, with no list or task caps published; work and school use needs a qualifying Microsoft 365 licence with Exchange Online.
Plans: Free with a personal Microsoft account; included in Microsoft 365 Family and Personal, and in Business Essentials, Business Premium, E1 to E5, F2 and Education A1 to A5 plans that carry Exchange Online.
Integrations_Note: Outlook tasks and flagged email, Planner assigned tasks, Teams, Microsoft Launcher, Power Automate and Zapier; the Microsoft Graph To Do API covers lists, tasks, checklist items and linked resources for personal and work accounts.
Hosting: Stored and synced in Exchange Online, so work and school data follows the Microsoft 365 tenant’s data location; personal accounts use Microsoft’s consumer cloud with no choice. No on-premise edition: on-premise Exchange mailboxes have been unsupported since March 2021.
Security: Encrypted at rest on Exchange servers and in transit. Work accounts inherit Microsoft 365 compliance commitments (ISO 27001, ISO 27018, GDPR, EU Data Boundary), Entra ID sign-in with SSO and MFA, per-user licence control and Purview eDiscovery; To Do has no admin console of its own.
Calendar_Sync: No calendar view or feed. In new Outlook and Outlook on the web, tasks can be dragged from the My Day pane onto the Outlook calendar as a time block (one-way). No Google Calendar sync.
Data_Out: No in-app export. Personal users export the whole mailbox to PST from desktop Outlook; admins export tasks as PST via Purview content search. The Microsoft Graph To Do API reads and writes lists, tasks and checklist items. No importers.
Platforms: Web, iOS, Android, Windows and macOS, plus Outlook (web, new Outlook, mobile) and Teams. No Linux app.
AI: No AI inside the To Do app. Microsoft 365 Copilot Premium users can query and edit To Do tasks through the Planner Agent since July 2026; Microsoft states prompts, responses and Graph data are not used to train foundation models.
Value_for_money_Review: Entirely free with a personal Microsoft account and already paid for in most Microsoft 365 work plans.
Ease_of_use_Review: My Day, smart lists and steps are learnt in minutes, and flagged Outlook email turns up as tasks without setup.
Enterprise_features_Review: Work accounts inherit Entra ID sign-in, licence control and Purview eDiscovery, but To Do itself has no team admin or roles.
Interface_flexibility_Review: Lists, My Day and smart lists only: no board, calendar view, custom fields or automation inside the app.
Data_control_Review: Tasks live in the Exchange Online mailbox under Microsoft 365 certifications and tenant data location; personal accounts get no region choice.
Portability_Review: No export button; data leaves through an Outlook PST export, admin eDiscovery or the Graph API, and there are no importers.
Summary: Microsoft To Do is a plain personal task list built by the former Wunderlist team and given away with every Microsoft account. It suits people who live in Outlook and want their own tasks, flagged email and assigned Planner tasks in one place. Tasks sit in lists and groups, with steps, notes, due dates, reminders, recurrence and file attachments; My Day is a daily shortlist that empties each night. There is no board, calendar view, timeline, custom field or automation inside the app. Lists can be shared, but there is no assignment workflow worth the name. There is nothing to buy. Personal accounts get everything free, and organisations get To Do with any Microsoft 365 plan that includes an Exchange Online mailbox; on-premise Exchange is not supported. Tasks are stored in the user’s Exchange Online mailbox, so work accounts inherit Microsoft 365 encryption, certifications and tenant data location, and admins can find tasks with Purview eDiscovery. Copilot Premium users can read and edit To Do tasks through the Planner Agent since July 2026. Leaving is awkward: there is no export button, only a whole-mailbox PST from Outlook or the Graph API. Microsoft’s task investment has shifted to Planner, and from December 2026 private tasks created in Planner stop landing in To Do.
Caveat: Microsoft is moving task management towards Planner: Windows Latest called To Do effectively in maintenance mode in August 2026, and from December 2026 private tasks created in Planner no longer appear in To Do, though no retirement has been announced.

Name: monday work management
Vendor: monday.com Ltd. Publicly listed on Nasdaq (MNDY); headquartered in Tel Aviv, Israel.
Market_Evidence: monday.com reported fiscal 2025 revenue of $1,232.0 million, up 27%, with 4,281 customers above $50,000 in annual recurring revenue, per its results release of 9 February 2026.
Price_Note: Basic, per seat per month billed annually; $12 billed monthly. Seats are sold in buckets: a 3-seat minimum, then multiples of 5, so a team of 4 buys 5 seats and a team of 6 buys 10.
Free_Plan_Note: Free for up to 2 seats, 3 boards and 3 docs with 8 column types; no timeline, calendar, automations, integrations or guests.
Plans: Free (up to 2 seats); Basic $9 annual or $12 monthly; Standard $12 annual or $14 monthly; Pro $19 annual or $24 monthly; Enterprise by quote. All paid plans have a 3-seat minimum.
Integrations_Note: monday.com claims 850+ integrations and marketplace apps, including Slack, Microsoft Teams, Outlook, Gmail, Google Calendar, Salesforce, HubSpot, Jira, GitHub, Zoom and Zapier; integrations start on Standard with 250 actions a month. A public GraphQL API with webhooks is available.
Hosting: AWS in three regions: United States, European Union (Germany) and Asia Pacific (Australia). The region is set automatically from the first user’s location and cannot be changed later; only EU Enterprise accounts keep all customer data, including sub-processors, inside the EU. No self-managed or on-premise edition.
Security: SOC 1 Type II, SOC 2 Type II, SOC 3, ISO/IEC 27001, 27017, 27018, 27032 and 27701, CSA STAR, TX-RAMP; HIPAA BAA available. SAML SSO, SCIM, audit log and session management on Enterprise; Guardian add-on (Enterprise only) adds tenant-level encryption and BYOK.
Calendar_Sync: Google Calendar and Outlook integration recipes from Standard. Board dates can be pushed one way, or two recipes combined so board items create events and new events create items; each run counts against the plan’s monthly integration actions.
Data_Out: Board export to Excel with optional updates and subitems (subitem updates excluded), up to 100,000 items per board; account-wide zip of all boards with uploaded files, run by admins once every 24 hours, excluding Workdocs, dashboards and archived boards. Workdocs export separately to PDF, Word or Markdown. Public GraphQL API with webhooks; Excel, CSV and other-tool importers.
Platforms: Web, iOS, Android, desktop apps for macOS and Windows.
AI: AI columns, AI agents, meeting notetaker and the monday vibe app builder on paid plans, metered by monthly AI credits (1,000, 2,000 and 3,000 on Basic, Standard and Pro; custom on Enterprise). monday.com states customer data is not used to train AI models, and admins can turn AI features off.
Value_for_money_Review: A 3-seat minimum and seat buckets; timeline needs Standard at $12 and time tracking needs Pro at $19.
Ease_of_use_Review: Colour-coded boards and templates get a team working on day one; cross-board structures take planning.
Enterprise_features_Review: SAML SSO, SCIM, audit log, multi-level permissions, portfolios and resource management, all on Enterprise only.
Interface_flexibility_Review: More than 30 column types, many board views, dashboards across up to 50 boards, automations and an apps framework.
Data_control_Review: US, EU (Germany) or Australian hosting, strict EU residency and BYOK through the Guardian add-on on Enterprise.
Portability_Review: Boards export to Excel with updates; admins get a zip of all boards and files; a full GraphQL API.
Summary: monday work management is the core product of monday.com, alongside the separate CRM, dev and service products built on the same platform. It is sold to teams of any type that want to model their own process rather than adopt a fixed project method. Everything lives on boards: rows are items, columns are typed fields such as status, people, date or formula, and the same board can be shown as a table, Kanban, timeline, Gantt chart, calendar or chart. Automations, dashboards and Workdocs connect boards together. There is no native Scrum layer in this product; sprints are sold separately in monday dev. The free plan is for 2 seats and 3 boards, so it is a trial in practice. Every paid plan starts at 3 seats and is sold in seat buckets. Basic at $9 a seat lacks timeline, calendar, automations and integrations, so most teams need Standard at $12; time tracking, private boards, dependencies and workload sit on Pro at $19. AI runs on monthly credits (1,000 on Basic, 2,000 on Standard, 3,000 on Pro), with more available to buy. Data is hosted on AWS in the US, Germany or Australia, with the region set by where the account is opened, and monday.com holds SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001, 27017, 27018 and 27701 certificates. SSO, SCIM, audit logs and strict EU residency are Enterprise features, and the Guardian add-on adds tenant keys and BYOK. monday.com states customer data is not used to train AI models. Boards export to Excel and the GraphQL API is complete, but Workdocs and dashboards are left out of the account export.
Caveat: The 3-seat minimum and fixed seat buckets mean the bill is often higher than the per-seat price suggests: a team that falls between bucket sizes pays for the next bucket up, and exceeding a bucket auto-upgrades the plan.

Name: Notion
Vendor: Notion Labs, Inc. Privately held and venture-funded; headquartered in San Francisco, United States.
Market_Evidence: Notion reported passing 100 million users in August 2024 (Notion blog, 3 September 2024), and CNBC reported about $500 million in annual revenue in September 2025.
Price_Note: Plus, per member per month billed annually; $12 billed monthly. Guests are free; there is no seat minimum.
Free_Plan_Note: Free is unlimited for one person, but a workspace with 2 or more members hits a block limit; 10 guests, 5 MB uploads, 7 days of page history and only a trial of Notion AI.
Plans: Free; Plus $10 yearly or $12 monthly; Business $20 yearly or $24 monthly; Enterprise by quote. Prices per member per month; Custom Agents cost $10 per 1,000 Notion credits on Business and Enterprise.
Integrations_Note: Connections for Slack, Google Drive, GitHub, Jira, Asana, Figma, Zoom, Salesforce and Microsoft Teams, with richer synced connections on Business; Zapier and Make cover the rest. Public REST API and webhooks, plus Workers and a CLI on the 2026 developer platform.
Hosting: AWS, US (Oregon) by default; data residency on Enterprise in the EU (Frankfurt), Japan (Tokyo) or Korea (Seoul) at no extra charge. No self-managed or on-premise edition.
Security: SOC 2, ISO/IEC 27001, 27018 and 27701, ISMAP, BSI C5; HIPAA BAA on Enterprise. SAML SSO and domain verification on Business; SCIM, audit log, granular admin roles, DLP and SIEM connections on Enterprise. Enterprise Key Management (customer-managed AWS KMS key, revocable by the customer) is in beta early access for selected Enterprise customers.
Calendar_Sync: The Notion Calendar app (macOS, Windows, iOS) connects Google and iCloud calendars and shows up to 20 Notion databases beside them, with two-way edits to dates and titles; Notion items cannot be shown inside Google, iCloud or Outlook calendars.
Data_Out: Page or workspace export as Markdown with CSV for databases, or HTML (including comments), with uploaded files; workspace PDF and subpage PDF export on Business and Enterprise; scheduled export API in beta on Enterprise. Public REST API and webhooks; importers for Asana, Trello, Confluence, monday.com, Evernote, Google Docs, Word, CSV and Markdown.
Platforms: Web, macOS, Windows, iOS, Android; Notion Calendar for macOS, Windows and iOS; web clipper extensions.
AI: Notion Agent (chat, generation, autofill), AI Meeting Notes, enterprise search across connected apps and research mode on Business and Enterprise, trial-only on Free and Plus; Custom Agents and Workers consume Notion credits at $10 per 1,000. Notion states customer data is not used to train models by Notion or its AI subprocessors; providers retain data for 30 days except on Enterprise (zero retention).
Value_for_money_Review: Free is generous for one person and Plus is $10, but full AI, SSO and Agents need Business at $20.
Ease_of_use_Review: Writing a page is instant; building a working task system from blank databases takes deliberate design.
Enterprise_features_Review: SAML SSO on Business; SCIM, audit log, DLP and SIEM connections, residency and beta key management on Enterprise.
Interface_flexibility_Review: Table, board, timeline, calendar, list, gallery, chart and form views, relations, database automations and an API.
Data_control_Review: Residency in the US, EU, Japan or Korea on Enterprise; customer-managed keys exist only as a beta for selected Enterprise customers.
Portability_Review: Any plan exports the whole workspace to Markdown, CSV or HTML with files; importers cover Asana, Trello and Confluence.
Summary: Notion combines documents, wikis and databases in one editor, so a project plan, its meeting notes and the task list behind it can live on the same page. It is used both by individuals and by whole companies as their internal knowledge base and planning tool. Everything is a page made of blocks, and databases are pages whose rows are pages. A task database can be shown as a table, board, timeline with dependencies, calendar, list, gallery or chart, and linked to other databases through relations. Notion supplies templates rather than a fixed task model, so assignment, status and recurrence are whatever a team builds. There is no time tracking. Free suits a single person; teams of two or more hit the block limit. Plus at $10 removes it. Since 13 May 2025 full Notion AI (the Notion Agent, meeting notes and enterprise search) comes only with Business at $20 and Enterprise, and Custom Agents are billed separately at $10 per 1,000 credits. Business also adds SAML SSO and private teamspaces. Notion holds SOC 2 and ISO 27001, 27018 and 27701, and offers data residency in the US, EU, Japan or Korea on Enterprise; customer-managed keys (Enterprise Key Management) are still a beta for selected Enterprise customers. It states customer data is not used to train AI models; LLM providers keep data 30 days except on Enterprise, where retention is zero. Workspace export to Markdown, CSV and HTML with uploaded files makes leaving realistic, though relations and views do not survive.
Caveat: Notion AI is now bundled only into Business and Enterprise, and agents are metered by credits; teams on Plus get a trial, not ongoing AI, so the real comparison price is often $20 rather than $10.

Name: Smartsheet

Market_Evidence: Smartsheet’s last public results, for the quarter to 31 October 2024, showed annualised recurring revenue of $1.133 billion and 2,137 customers above $100,000 a year (SEC filing, 5 December 2024); in November 2026 it cites over 3,000 employees and use in more than 85% of Fortune 500 companies.
Price_Note: Pro, per Member per month billed annually; $12 billed monthly. Pro is limited to 10 Members and is sold only to new customers; Business ($19) requires at least 3 Members.
Free_Plan_Note: No free plan; a 30-day free trial with no credit card. Contributors (editors who do not create sheets) and viewers are free on paid plans.
Plans: Pro $9 yearly or $12 monthly (1 to 10 Members); Business $19 yearly or $24 monthly (3+ Members); Enterprise by quote (10+ Members); Advanced Work Management by quote. Prices per Member per month.
Integrations_Note: Microsoft 365, Google Workspace and Slack on every plan; Power BI, Tableau, Adobe Creative Cloud and AI connectors for Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini and Copilot from Business; Workday, ServiceNow, HubSpot and Docusign on Enterprise; the pricing page counts nearly 100 more. Hosting: AWS: US East (default), EU (Germany with Ireland backup) and Australia through Smartsheet Regions; Smartsheet Gov on AWS GovCloud West. Usage and account data are not covered by residency. No self-managed edition.
Security: SOC 2, ISO/IEC 27001, 27701 and 42001, HIPAA BAA on Enterprise; Smartsheet Gov holds a FedRAMP Moderate authorisation (JAB) and DISA IL4. Basic SSO and Admin Center on all plans; SAML SSO, directory integrations and user provisioning on Enterprise; event reporting, data retention, data egress and CMEK are Enterprise add-ons.
Calendar_Sync: Publish a sheet’s dates to Google Calendar (up to 600 rows, Pro and above) or as an iCal feed (Business and Enterprise), both one-way; a Google calendar can be overlaid read-only on a sheet. REST API from Business.
Platforms: Web, iOS, Android; add-ins for Outlook and Gmail.
AI: Smart Assist, AI columns, AI dashboard builder, formula generation and data analysis on all plans; connectors for external AI tools (Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, Copilot) from Business. Smartsheet states it never allows a third party to train foundation models on customer data.

Ease_of_use_Review: The grid feels like a spreadsheet, but formulas, cross-sheet references and workflows reward trained builders.
Enterprise_features_Review: SAML SSO, directory provisioning, Enterprise Plan Manager, access controls, FedRAMP for Gov, CMEK and event-reporting add-ons.
Interface_flexibility_Review: Grid, Gantt, board, calendar, table and timeline views, dashboards, reports, forms, automations and no-code WorkApps.
Data_control_Review: US, EU (Germany) or Australian regions, a GovCloud edition and customer-managed encryption keys as an add-on.
Portability_Review: Sheets export to Excel with comments; scheduled backups need Business, and the API is not on Pro.
Summary: Smartsheet looks like a spreadsheet but behaves like a project tool: each row is a task with owners, dates, dependencies and attachments. It is bought mostly by large organisations and their PMOs, and by operations teams that already think in rows and columns. A sheet can be shown as a grid, Gantt chart, board, calendar or table, and reports and dashboards roll many sheets together. Formulas, cross-sheet references, forms, approval workflows and no-code WorkApps let teams build their own systems. Much of the advanced range is sold separately: Resource Management (which holds time tracking), Dynamic View from $125 a month, Data Shuttle from $100 a month, DataMesh, Calendar App and Brandfolder. There is no free plan. Pro at $9 suits a small team of up to 10 Members but lacks the API, timeline view and scheduled backups. Business at $19 needs 3 Members and adds those, plus unlimited automations and workload tracking. SAML SSO, portfolios and directory integration require Enterprise. Data can sit in the US, the EU (Germany) or Australia through Smartsheet Regions, and a separate Smartsheet Gov runs on AWS GovCloud. Smartsheet lists SOC 2, ISO 27001, 27701 and 42001, with a FedRAMP Moderate authorisation for Smartsheet Gov, and says third parties never train foundation models on customer data. Backups on Business and above are Excel workbooks with comments and uploaded attachments, but formulas, reports and dashboards do not travel.
Caveat: Smartsheet has been private since January 2025 and no longer publishes revenue; it dropped its free plan and moved to a Member and Contributor licence model, so older comparisons describe plans that no longer exist.

Name: Trello
Vendor: Atlassian. Publicly listed (NASDAQ: TEAM); founded in Sydney, Australia, now incorporated in the United States. Trello is run as part of Atlassian’s business-teams products.
Market_Evidence: Trello announced 50 million registered users in 2019 (VentureBeat, October 2019) and has been a product line of public company Atlassian since 2017; no newer official user count is published.
Price_Note: Standard, per user per month billed annually; $6 billed monthly.
Free_Plan_Note: Unlimited cards and Power-Ups with 10 boards and 10 collaborators per Workspace, 10MB per file and 250 automation runs a month; boards go view-only above 10 collaborators.
Plans: Free $0; Standard $5 per user per month annually ($6 monthly); Premium $10 annually ($12.50 monthly); Enterprise $17.50 per user per month billed annually only, quoted for 50 users with lower rates at higher volumes.
Integrations_Note: Trello’s own guide counts upwards of 200 Power-Ups, including Slack, Google Drive, Jira, Microsoft Teams and Zapier; a public REST API with webhooks is available on every plan, plus an MCP server for AI tools.
Hosting: Atlassian-run on AWS; user content is stored in US AWS regions. Trello is not covered by Atlassian’s data residency programme and has no self-managed or on-premise edition.
Security: Covered by Atlassian’s SOC 2 Type II reports and ISO/IEC 27001 and 27018 certifications. SSO and user provisioning come through Atlassian Guard, included on Enterprise and a separate subscription from $4 per user per month otherwise.
Calendar_Sync: Planner (web and desktop) connects up to 10 Google or Outlook calendar accounts, displays their events and writes focus-time blocks to them; card due dates publish one way through the Calendar Power-Up’s iCal feed.
Data_Out: Board export as JSON on all plans (comments only within the latest 1,000 actions); CSV board export and Workspace export in JSON and CSV, optionally with raw attachments in a ZIP, need Premium. Public REST API and webhooks on all plans.
Platforms: Web, iOS, Android, macOS and Windows desktop apps; email-to-board and Slack capture into the Inbox.
AI: Atlassian AI on Standard, Premium and Enterprise, switched on by default with admin opt-out: board generation, checklist generation, natural-language due dates, Smart Schedule and image generation. Atlassian’s data contribution FAQ says Trello in-app data is not yet used for its August 2026 AI-training programme until settings exist for Trello.
Value_for_money_Review: A free plan for 10 collaborators and $5 Standard, but calendar, timeline and table views need $10 Premium.
Ease_of_use_Review: Lists and cards on a board are learnt in minutes; the model has barely changed since 2011.
Enterprise_features_Review: Enterprise adds SSO and provisioning through Atlassian Guard and SOC 2 reports, but little portfolio reporting.
Interface_flexibility_Review: Five extra views, custom fields and Butler automation exist, though most depth arrives through 200 Power-Ups.
Data_control_Review: SOC 2 and ISO 27001 under Atlassian, but content sits in US AWS regions with no residency choice.
Portability_Review: JSON board export on every plan is capped at 1,000 actions; CSV and full Workspace export need Premium.
Summary: Trello is the board most people meet first: lists running left to right, cards moving between them. Atlassian sells it to any team that wants shared visual task lists without the weight of a project tool such as Jira. Cards carry checklists, due dates, labels, attachments and custom fields, and Butler automation moves them by rule. Power-Ups add almost everything else, from Gantt charts to time tracking, which Trello does not build in. Calendar, Timeline, Table, Dashboard and Map views belong to Premium, and the Timeline has no dependencies. Planner pulls Google or Outlook events beside your cards and schedules focus time back into the calendar. The free plan is generous on cards and Power-Ups but, since May 2024, a free Workspace with more than 10 collaborators (members, guests and pending invites) turns view-only. Standard at $5 removes the board and collaborator caps; most teams wanting more than boards will need Premium at $10. Content is held in Atlassian’s US AWS regions, with SOC 2 and ISO 27001 coverage. AI features (board generation, checklists, smart scheduling) are on by default on paid plans. Export is JSON per board for everyone, CSV and Workspace exports with attachments for Premium, and the public API is open on all plans.
Caveat: Since 20 May 2024, free Workspaces with more than 10 collaborators become view-only and their automations stop; no later relaxation of this limit has been announced.

Name: Airtable
Vendor: Airtable. Owned by Bending Spoons S.p.A. (Milan, Italy; Nasdaq: BSP) since its acquisition closed on 4 September 2026; headquartered in San Francisco, United States.
Market_Evidence: Bending Spoons agreed in August 2026 to buy Airtable at an enterprise value of $1.285 billion, citing annual recurring revenue of about $480 million in June 2026 (SEC 6-K, 4 August 2026); Airtable’s about page cites 500,000 companies and 10 million active users (November 2026).
Price_Note: Team, per seat per month billed annually; $24 billed monthly. Only users with edit rights are billed; read-only collaborators are free.
Free_Plan_Note: Free covers up to 5 editors, unlimited bases at 1,000 records each, 100 automation runs and 1,000 API calls a month; no timeline, Gantt or extensions.
Plans: Free; Team $20 annual or $24 monthly; Business $45 annual or $54 monthly; Enterprise Scale by quote. Prices per seat per month.
Integrations_Note: Native sync and automation connectors for Slack, Gmail, Google Drive, Google Calendar, Outlook, Salesforce, Jira, GitHub, Zendesk, Box, Snowflake, Databricks and Tableau, plus Marketplace extensions and an MCP server for Claude and ChatGPT. Public REST API with webhooks on every plan, capped at 1,000 calls a month on Free.
Hosting: AWS, US by default; data residency in Europe or Australia on Enterprise Scale. No self-managed or on-premise edition.
Security: SOC 2 Type II, ISO/IEC 27001:2022 and 27701:2019, TX-RAMP Level 2; HIPAA support. SAML SSO on Business and Enterprise Scale; audit logs, Enterprise Key Management (AWS KMS) and data residency on Enterprise Scale.
Calendar_Sync: One-way iCal subscription from a shared calendar view on all plans (external apps refresh on their own schedule, up to 24 hours). Google Calendar and Outlook Calendar sync integrations bring events into a table one way on paid plans; updating events from Airtable needs an automation.
Data_Out: CSV download per view (attachments as URLs; comments not included); XLSX and PDF only by converting the CSV. Snapshots restore a base inside Airtable. Public REST API and webhooks API on all plans; importers for CSV, Excel, Google Sheets and Smartsheet exports.
Platforms: Web, macOS and Windows desktop apps, iOS, Android.
AI: Omni assistant, AI fields, field agents and app building on all plans, metered by monthly credits: 500 per editor on Free, 15,000 per seat on Team, 20,000 on Business, 25,000 on Enterprise Scale. Models from OpenAI, Google, Anthropic and Meta (via Amazon Bedrock) and IBM. Airtable’s AI terms state neither Airtable nor its providers train on customer data; providers may keep inputs up to 30 days for abuse monitoring on Free and Team.
Value_for_money_Review: A free plan for 5 editors and 1,000 records a base, then $20 a seat, and $45 for SSO and admin.
Ease_of_use_Review: The grid is familiar at once, but linked tables, interfaces and automations ask for database thinking.
Enterprise_features_Review: SAML SSO and admin panel on Business; audit logs, EKM, residency and org units on Enterprise Scale.
Interface_flexibility_Review: Grid, Kanban, calendar, gallery, form, list, timeline and Gantt views, interfaces, automations, scripting and extensions.
Data_control_Review: US, EU or Australian residency and customer-owned AWS KMS keys, both on Enterprise Scale only.
Portability_Review: CSV per view only, without comments; the full REST API and webhooks are the real exit.
Summary: Airtable is a no-code database: each base holds linked tables of typed fields, and teams build their own trackers, content calendars and lightweight apps on top. It suits operations, marketing and product teams who outgrow spreadsheets but do not want a fixed project tool. Any table can be viewed as a grid, Kanban board, calendar, gallery, form, timeline or Gantt chart, and Interfaces turn bases into custom screens for people who should not see the raw data. Automations, scripting and the Omni AI assistant sit across the whole base. It is not a task manager out of the box: assignment, recurrence and time tracking have to be modelled. Free allows 5 editors and 1,000 records a base, which suits a trial or a small project. Team at $20 a seat raises that to 50,000 records with Gantt and timeline views; Business at $45 adds SSO, the admin panel and two-way sync between bases. AI runs on monthly credits (15,000 per seat on Team), with top-ups from $20 per 10,000. Airtable holds SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 and 27701 certificates. Data residency in the US, Europe or Australia and customer-managed keys are Enterprise Scale features, and its AI terms bar Airtable and its model providers from training on customer data. Export is CSV per view, so a full exit means using the API. Bending Spoons completed its purchase of Airtable on 4 September 2026 and let go a large part of the pre-acquisition team in October; it says nothing changes for customers’ plans or prices.
Caveat: Bending Spoons completed its $1.285 billion acquisition on 4 September 2026 and parted with a large share of the pre-acquisition team in October; it says plans, prices and service are unchanged, so check terms at renewal.

Name: Any.do
Vendor: Any.do Inc. and affiliates. Privately held; the privacy policy relies on Israel’s EU adequacy decision for data transfers, pointing to operations in Israel, but publishes no head office address.
Market_Evidence: Any.do’s homepage claims 50M+ people and 651K app-store reviews averaging 4.8 (checked November 2026); no revenue or headcount is published.
Price_Note: Premium, per person per month billed annually; $7.99 billed monthly. Teams is also $4.99 per member per month billed annually ($7.99 monthly).
Free_Plan_Note: The free Personal plan has unlimited tasks, subtasks and grocery lists with reminders, the calendar view and My Day, but no recurring tasks, WhatsApp, colour tags, location reminders or AI.
Plans: Personal is free; Premium is $4.99 a month billed annually or $7.99 monthly; Family is $8.33 a month billed annually or $9.99 monthly for four members; Teams is $4.99 per member per month billed annually or $7.99 monthly, with no stated minimum.
Integrations_Note: Google, Outlook and iCloud calendars, WhatsApp, Gmail, Slack, Zoom, Siri and Apple Reminders, Zapier, Make, Pabbly and Integrately; an MCP server for ChatGPT and Claude, but no documented public REST API or webhooks.
Hosting: “Any.do’s servers”; no provider or region is published and there is no region choice or self-managed edition.
Security: Encryption in transit stated; email verification codes for new sign-ins; GDPR rights and Israeli adequacy covered in the privacy policy. No certifications, SSO, SCIM or audit log are published; Teams has admin tools and permissions.
Calendar_Sync: Google, Outlook or iCloud (one account) on web and desktop, and device calendars on iOS and Android, mirrored into the calendar view on all plans. The help centre says events can be added, edited and deleted from Any.do with invitations sent through the native provider, while a 2026 Any.do blog post says the sync is read-based for events and that tasks reach Google Calendar only when scheduled as time blocks. No documented route for calendar edits to update a task.
Data_Out: Boards export to CSV, Excel or PDF on Family and Teams; personal lists print to PDF, and archived personal tasks export as CSV by email. Comments and attachments are not documented as included. No public REST API; an MCP server with OAuth. Importers from Trello, Asana, ClickUp, Monday and Todoist on Family and Teams.
Platforms: Web, iOS, iPadOS, Android, macOS, Windows, Apple Watch and Wear OS, plus Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Safari extensions and a Gmail add-on.
AI: AI features on Premium and above, plus a beta MCP connector for ChatGPT, Claude and other agents on all plans. The privacy policy’s no-training commitment is stated for Google Workspace API data only; no AI provider is named.
Value_for_money_Review: Unlimited tasks free, then $4.99 a month for Premium or per Teams member, with no seat minimum.
Ease_of_use_Review: Lists, My Day and a calendar beside them are clear within minutes; boards and automations only appear on Family and Teams.
Enterprise_features_Review: Teams has admin tools and permissions, but no SSO, audit log, certifications or published security documentation.
Interface_flexibility_Review: Teams adds Kanban, table, calendar and Gantt views, custom fields and rule automations; personal plans stay list and calendar only.
Data_control_Review: No hosting provider, region or certification is published, and only encryption in transit is stated.
Portability_Review: Boards export to CSV or Excel on Family and Teams, but personal lists print only to PDF; no REST API.
Summary: Any.do is a to-do list and daily planner that puts tasks next to the events of your existing calendar, with reminders that can arrive on WhatsApp. It is aimed at individuals and households first, with a Teams plan for small groups who want shared boards. Personal plans offer lists, subtasks, My Day and a calendar view that mirrors Google, Outlook or iCloud events. Family adds shared boards and a grocery list. Teams adds Kanban, table, calendar and Gantt views, custom fields, task chat, rule automations and time tracking, though the help centre documents few details of the last two. The free plan has no task cap but holds back recurring tasks, WhatsApp reminders, tags and AI. Premium is $4.99 a month billed annually, and Teams is the same per member with no stated minimum, which makes it one of the cheaper shared boards. Importers from Trello, Asana, ClickUp, Monday and Todoist need Family or Teams. Data protection is thinly documented: the vendor names no hosting provider, region or certification, and states encryption in transit only. An MCP server lets ChatGPT and Claude read and edit tasks on every plan. Leaving is easier from boards, which export to CSV or Excel, than from personal lists, which print to PDF or export archived tasks as CSV.
Caveat: Any.do publishes no hosting location, security certification or AI training policy beyond Google API data, so organisations with compliance needs have little to check.

Name: Basecamp
Vendor: 37signals LLC. Privately held and self-funded, based in Chicago, United States; also makes HEY and Fizzy.
Market_Evidence: Basecamp’s homepage (November 2026) claims 84 million accounts and 60 million projects created to date, and says nearly a million people and organisations rely on it daily.
Price_Note: Flat rate, not per user: Freelancer is $29 a month for the whole account (up to 5 users, 3 active projects), billed monthly only; annual billing exists only on Pro Unlimited ($199 a month billed annually, $329 monthly).
Free_Plan_Note: Basecamp Personal is free for one project, three users and 1 GB of storage, without templates, time tracking or multiple tools per project.
Plans: Basecamp Personal, free (1 project, 3 users); Freelancer $29/month (3 active projects, 5 users, 10 GB); Pro $79/month (8 projects, 10 users, 25 GB); Pro Plus $99/month (12 projects, 15 users, 100 GB, time tracking); Pro Unlimited $199/month billed annually or $329 monthly (unlimited projects and users, 1 TB, Admin Pro Pack).
Integrations_Note: The integrations directory lists roughly 100 third-party tools, mostly time trackers (Harvest, Clockify, Everhour), Zapier, Zoho Flow and Unito; there is a public REST API with webhooks, official SDKs, a CLI and an MCP connector for ChatGPT and Claude.
Hosting: 37signals’ own servers in colocation facilities, primarily in the United States; no EU or other region choice and no self-managed edition.
Security: No SOC 2 or ISO 27001; PCI DSS SAQ A self-assessment, published CSA CAIQ v4.1 and HECVAT 4 questionnaires, DPA on request. No SSO, SAML or SCIM; Google sign-in and 2FA available, with enforced 2FA and permission restrictions in the Admin Pro Pack on Pro Unlimited.
Calendar_Sync: One-way iCal subscription of the global or a project calendar (events, or events plus assignments) into Google, Apple, Outlook or HEY; updates can take a few hours. All plans.
Data_Out: Account owners can export the whole account, selected projects or Ping conversations as an HTML archive including files and comments; timesheets export as CSV; full REST API with webhooks, SDKs and a CLI. The HTML export cannot be re-imported.
Platforms: Web; iOS and Android apps; desktop apps for macOS and Windows; installable PWA in Chrome (including Linux), Safari and Edge.
AI: No built-in AI features process customer content. Users can connect their own agents through the CLI or the ChatGPT and Claude MCP connectors on all plans; 37signals says content is not used to train AI models.
Value_for_money_Review: Flat pricing from $29 a month for five users gets cheap per head, but project caps and a one-project free plan bite.
Ease_of_use_Review: Every project is the same toolbox of messages, to-dos, cards and chat, so new people and clients orient in minutes.
Enterprise_features_Review: The vendor states it supports no SSO or SAML, no SCIM, and only the top package adds permission restrictions and enforced 2FA.
Interface_flexibility_Review: Lists, card tables, a calendar and hill charts, but no custom fields, automations or dashboards.
Data_control_Review: Runs on 37signals’ own hardware in the United States, with no SOC 2 or ISO 27001, only self-assessed questionnaires.
Portability_Review: An owner-only HTML export with files covers every project and the API is complete, but tasks never export as CSV or JSON.
Summary: Basecamp organises work as projects, each a page of tools: a message board, to-do lists, a Kanban card table, group chat, docs and files, and scheduled check-ins. It is built for small companies, agencies and anyone who invites clients into the work. Basecamp 5, released in 2026, added subtasks, a global calendar, account-wide Everything pages and Markdown in documents. Planning stays deliberately light: hill charts show progress by feel, and Lineup places whole projects on a 13-week timeline. There are no custom fields, automations, dependencies or dashboards, and time tracking is a manual timesheet. Pricing is a flat monthly fee for the account rather than per seat. Freelancer at $29 covers five users and three active projects; Pro at $79 and Pro Plus at $99 raise those to 10 and 15 users. Pro Unlimited, $199 a month billed annually, removes the caps and is the only package with annual billing and the Admin Pro Pack. Large teams pay little per head; a seven-person team with ten live projects already needs Pro Plus. Data sits on 37signals’ own servers in the United States after its 2023 exit from the public cloud, with no residency choice and no SOC 2 or ISO 27001 certificate. There are no built-in AI features, and the privacy policy says content is not used to train models. Leaving means an HTML archive of every project plus files, or the public API.
Caveat: Basecamp’s packages changed during 2026 and its help centre still names plans (Studio, Unlimited) that no longer appear on the pricing page; only Pro Unlimited can be billed annually.

Name: Bitrix24
Vendor: Alaio Inc. of Alexandria, Virginia, USA contracts with most customers; Alaio Cloud Limited of Limassol, Cyprus with European ones; the terms are governed by Virginia law. Privately held. The Record reported in December 2023 that Bitrix24’s parent company, 1C-Bitrix, is headquartered in Russia; Bitrix24 did not respond to the report, and the vendor does not publish who owns the Alaio entities.
Market_Evidence: Bitrix24’s about page (read November 2026) claims more than 15 million organisations, 600+ staff in 12 countries and 960+ partners in 90+ countries; the organisation count includes free sign-ups.
Price_Note: Flat rate per organisation, not per user: Basic is $49 a month billed annually ($69 monthly) for up to 5 users; Standard $99 ($144) covers 50 users and Professional $199 ($289) covers 100. No per-user plan exists.
Free_Plan_Note: Unlimited users (the help centre, updated October 2026, confirms; the pricing page markets it as for 1 to 2 users), 5 GB, one admin, task lists, Kanban and a limited Gantt view, but no task time tracking, project views or REST API; idle accounts are deleted after 50 days.
Plans: Free; Basic $49, Standard $99, Professional $199 and Enterprise from $399 (250 users, tiers up to 10,000 users at $7,999) a month billed annually; each paid plan also has a Vibe+ version ($59, $120, $240, Enterprise from $480) adding REST API, unlimited Market apps and unlimited AI. Self-hosted: Business $3,590 (50 users) and Enterprise $24,990 (1,000+), renewed yearly at 50%.
Integrations_Note: Bitrix24 Market lists 760+ apps (700+ in a September 2026 vendor blog) plus built-in Google Docs, Office 365 and telephony connectors; the REST API with inbound and outbound webhooks is only on Vibe+ plans, and Essentials plans cap Market apps.
Hosting: AWS in the USA (Virginia) or the EU (Frankfurt, Germany); EU domains such as bitrix24.eu, .de, .fr, .it and .pl are hosted in Frankfurt, bitrix24.com in the USA. Enterprise adds two geographically distributed data centres. A self-hosted edition runs on PHP and MySQL on Linux, Unix or Windows servers.
Security: The security page cites AWS’s ISO 27001, SOC 1/2/3, PCI DSS and HIPAA, not certifications held by Bitrix24 itself; TLS, two-step authentication and IP restrictions on all plans; SAML SSO and 180-day login history on Enterprise only; signed GDPR DPA for EU customers.
Calendar_Sync: Two-way real-time sync of Bitrix24 calendar events with Google Calendar, Apple iCloud and Microsoft Office 365 on every plan, plus CalDAV connections and macOS Calendar via CalDAV; tasks with deadlines appear in the Bitrix24 calendar but sync is documented for events.
Data_Out: Task lists export to Excel with selected or all fields, and import from CSV; daily backups kept 7 days (30 on Enterprise) with restore on Standard and above; REST API and webhooks only on Vibe+ plans after 30 November 2026.
Platforms: Web, iOS, Android, and desktop apps for Windows, macOS and Linux.
AI: CoPilot (task descriptions, checklists, summaries, project agents) on every plan, limited on Essentials and unlimited on Vibe+ Standard and above. The AI terms name OpenAI as provider with requests processed in the USA, say AI tools may be switched on automatically, and allow AI providers to use content for development and improvement, while marketing pages say data is not used for training.
Value_for_money_Review: Free with no user cap, then flat fees: $99 a month covers 50 users; Scrum and full time tracking need $199.
Ease_of_use_Review: Tasks sit inside a crowded suite of CRM, chat, sites and HR tools, and new users face a dense menu.
Enterprise_features_Review: SAML SSO, login history and branch accounts only on Enterprise from $399; certifications cited are AWS’s, not Bitrix24’s own.
Interface_flexibility_Review: List, Kanban, planner, calendar, Gantt and Scrum views, automation rules, workflows, BI Builder and a 760-app marketplace.
Data_control_Review: A self-hosted edition, or AWS in Virginia or Frankfurt, but the AI terms let providers use content and ownership is unpublished.
Portability_Review: Task lists export to Excel and import from CSV, but the REST API now needs a Vibe+ plan.
Summary: Bitrix24 is a business suite in which tasks and projects share a workspace with CRM, chat, video calls, documents, sites and HR tools. It is sold to small and mid-sized organisations that want one vendor for most of their software. The tasks module offers list, Kanban, planner, calendar and Gantt views with four dependency types, plus subtasks, checklists, templates, recurring tasks and automation rules. Scrum boards, full time tracking and workload reports arrive on Professional. The breadth is also the cost: the task manager is one item in a long menu, and the interface carries every other module with it. Pricing is a flat monthly fee per organisation. The free plan has no user cap but stops at 5 GB and one admin. Standard at $99 a month (annual) covers 50 users; Professional at $199 covers 100. Since 1 September 2026 each plan has a cheaper Essentials version without REST API, MCP server or unlimited AI, and a Vibe+ version with them; monthly and quarterly customers move to Essentials limits on 30 November 2026, annual ones at their next renewal. Cloud data sits on AWS in Virginia or Frankfurt, chosen by the account’s regional domain, and an EU DPA is offered. The self-hosted edition (from $3,590, renewed yearly at half price) includes source code. CoPilot AI is on all plans, sends requests to OpenAI in the USA, and the terms let AI providers use content for development. Leaving the cloud means Excel exports or the API on a Vibe+ plan.
Caveat: The plan line-up changed on 1 September 2026: from 30 November 2026 Essentials plans lose the REST API and MCP server and get capped AI and Market apps unless the customer pays for Vibe+ (annual plans bought before 1 September keep their terms until they end). The security page still cites Safe Harbor and lists only AWS’s certifications.
